chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a doze and two dozes,
He said: I do not know what a doze and two dozes are.
Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, says: “Rather, the human being is fully aware of himself.”
Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Whoever experiences the taste of sleep, then wudu (ablution) has become obligatory upon him.

key_terms.الْخَفْقَةُ: a brief doze or nodding off
key_terms.الْخَفْقَتَيْنِ: two brief dozes; repeated light sleep
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for salat (prayer)
key_terms.بَصِيرَةٌ: inner awareness or insight regarding one’s own state
key_terms.طَعْمَ النَّوْمِ: the felt onset or actual experience of sleep

ai.seo_question: Does a light doze invalidate wudu (ablution) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal effect of sleep upon wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام refers the matter to a person’s own awareness, citing the Qur’anic principle that the human being is aware of himself, and then transmits from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام that when one truly experiences sleep, wudu (ablution) becomes obligatory.
